mainTopic: Permitted uses of שביעית produce (the רבי יוסי vs. רבנן dispute), and how the sanctity of שביעית produce is transferred: through מקח only, or also through חילול
overview: The amud opens by finishing a dispute about how שביעית produce may be used. רבי יוסי explains that 'לכם' includes laundering, which every person needs, while 'לאכלה' excludes a remedy, which only the sick need. The גמרא then shows that a ברייתא forbidding only remedy, sprinkling, and emetic follows רבי יוסי, since the רבנן would also have listed soaking and laundering. Next, רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן disagree: does the holiness of שביעית produce transfer only through a purchase (מקח), or also through redemption (חילול)? Each brings a verse, and the גמרא explains what each one learns from the other's verse. A ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר: the holiness spreads to whatever is bought with the produce, while the produce itself stays holy. Because it keeps saying 'לקח' (he bought), it shows that purchase works and redemption does not. A second ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן, saying שביעית and מעשר שני produce can be redeemed (מתחללין) onto animals, with רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagreeing about live animals. רבא then begins to explain that dispute, and his statement continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יוסי explains which uses the verse includes and which it excludes
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי reconciles 'לכם' (an inclusion) with 'לאכלה' (an exclusion). Laundering is included because everyone needs it. A remedy is excluded because only sick people need it.
steps.simpleTranslation: I include laundering, which is equally relevant to every person, and I exclude a remedy, which is not equally relevant to every person.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוסי's answer to a question on the previous amud. The question was: if the verse says 'לאכלה' (for food), how can he permit laundering with שביעית produce?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse contains two words that pull in opposite directions. 'לכם' means 'for all your needs' and widens the permitted uses. 'לאכלה' means 'for food' and narrows them. רבי יוסי settles the tension with one test: is this a need that every person shares? Laundering passes the test, so it is allowed. A medical remedy fails it, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: I include (I learn from the verse that this case is added)
laundering
a medicinal poultice or remedy
equally relevant to every person

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume 'everything that is not eating is forbidden.' According to רבי יוסי, the line is whether a use is common to all people, not whether it is literally eating.

phrases.english: I include laundering
phrases.notes: This comes from the word 'לכם', which means for all your needs.

phrases.english: which is equal for every person,
and I exclude a remedy
which is not equal for every person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge to רבי יוסי on the previous amud: how can he permit laundering when the verse says 'לאכלה'?
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the two words of the verse between two different kinds of use (shared needs versus individual needs)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the verse says 'לאכלה', it seemed that only eating should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'לכם' includes universal needs like laundering. 'לאכלה' excludes non-universal needs like a remedy.

steps.title: Who is the author of the ברייתא about food, remedy, sprinkling, and emetic?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that lists forbidden uses of שביעית produce and asks which תנא wrote it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who taught what the Rabbis taught: 'For food' — and not for a remedy; 'for food' — and not for sprinkling; 'for food' — and not to make it into an emetic?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that lists three forbidden uses of שביעית produce. It asks whose opinion this ברייתא follows, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item in the ברייתא is a use that only some people need. Sprinkling wine for a pleasant smell is a luxury, and an emetic is medicine. The point to notice is what the list does not include: soaking and laundering.

keyTerms.meaning: Who is the תנא (author) of this teaching?
sprinkling wine in a room for a pleasant smell
an emetic, a drink that makes a person vomit
for food (from the פסוק about שביעית produce)

phrases.english: Who is the author of that which the Rabbis taught:
'For food' — and not for a remedy,
'for food' — and not for sprinkling,
'for food' — and not to make it into an emetic?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the רבי יוסי / רבנן dispute to identify the author of a different ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which side of the dispute this ברייתא follows.

steps.title: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי, because it leaves out soaking and laundering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא follows רבי יוסי. If it followed the רבנן, it would also have listed soaking and laundering as forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is it? רבי יוסי's. For if it were the Rabbis, there is also soaking and laundering (which they forbid and which should have been listed).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the author is רבי יוסי. It proves this from what the ברייתא leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן forbid soaking and laundering, so a ברייתא written by them would have mentioned those uses. Since the list stops at remedy, sprinkling, and emetic, it matches רבי יוסי. He permits laundering and forbids only uses that are not common to everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom?
for if
soaking (for example, soaking flax in water)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא that lists remedy, sprinkling, and emetic follows רבי יוסי, because the רבנן would also have forbidden soaking and laundering.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom? Rabbi Yosei.
For if it were the Rabbis,
there is also soaking and laundering (that should have been listed).
phrases.notes: The point is that the ברייתא didn't mention these, so why not?

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוסי — proven by the absence of soaking and laundering from the list.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר and רבי יוחנן disagree on how שביעית sanctity is transferred
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the sanctity of שביעית produce transfers only through a purchase (מקח). רבי יוחנן says it transfers through either a purchase or a redemption-style declaration (חילול).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: שביעית produce is deconsecrated only by way of purchase. רבי יוחנן said: both by way of purchase and by way of redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic opens. Two אמוראים disagree about the method by which the sanctity of שביעית produce moves onto something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מקח means buying something with the produce in a normal sale, so the sanctity passes onto what you bought. חילול means simply declaring that the sanctity moves onto coins, the way one redeems הקדש. רבי אלעזר accepts only the first method, and רבי יוחנן accepts both.

keyTerms.meaning: produce of the seventh (שמיטה) year, which has special sanctity
is deconsecrated (its sanctity transfers to something else)
by way of a purchase or sale
by way of redemption, a declaration of transfer

steps.confusionAlert: In both methods the sanctity does not disappear. It moves onto the new item or coins. The dispute is only about which method works.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שְׁבִיעִית מִתְחַלֶּלֶת אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ מִקָּח.
phrases.english: Sheviis produce is deconsecrated only by way of purchase.
And Rabbi Yochanan said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין דֶּרֶךְ מִקָּח בֵּין דֶּרֶךְ חִילּוּל.
phrases.english: both by way of purchase and by way of redemption.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אֵין שְׁבִיעִית מִתְחַלֶּלֶת אֶלָּא דֶּרֶךְ מִקָּח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic about how שביעית money and produce work.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר: only through מקח. רבי יוחנן: through מקח or חילול.
steps.whyThisMatters: This affects how שביעית produce can be exchanged, which connects to our משנה about buying a לולב in שביעית.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's source: the יובל verse placed next to 'when you sell'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר learns his rule from the fact that the verse about יובל is placed right next to the verse about selling. This shows that the transfer works through a sale, not through redemption.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is רבי אלעזר's reason? As it is written: 'In this year of יובל...', and right next to it: 'And when you sell a sale' — by way of purchase and not by way of redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רבי אלעזר's source and answers it from two neighboring verses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two verses that sit side by side can teach about each other (סמיכות). Since the verse about יובל, which carries the laws of שביעית, is followed by a verse about selling, רבי אלעזר concludes that the sanctity transfers only through a sale.

keyTerms.meaning: What is his reason?
and placed right next to it (a learning from adjacent verses)
the Jubilee year, which shares the laws of שביעית
a sale

phrases.english: What is Rabbi Elazar's reason?
As it is written: 'In this year of Yovel, etc.'
and next to it: 'And when you sell a sale',
by way of purchase and not by way of redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the verse source for the first opinion in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי אלעזר's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two verses placed side by side link שביעית/יובל produce to selling.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: יובל is called 'קודש', like הקדש
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן learns from the phrase 'it is קודש'. Just as הקדש can be transferred through either a purchase or a redemption, so can שביעית produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is רבי יוחנן's reason? As it is written: 'For it is יובל, it shall be holy.' Just as holy things transfer both by purchase and by redemption, so too שביעית produce transfers both by purchase and by redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives רבי יוחנן's source. This completes the presentation of the dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls יובל 'קודש', and רבי יוחנן reads this as a comparison to הקדש. הקדש can be redeemed through a declaration (חילול), not only through a sale. So שביעית produce can transfer through either method as well.

keyTerms.meaning: holy, consecrated (here compared to הקדש)
just as ... so too (a comparison formula)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר: only מקח, learned from the neighboring verse about selling. רבי יוחנן: both מקח and חילול, learned from the comparison to קודש.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan, what is his reason?
As it is written: 'For it is Yovel, it shall be holy.'

phrases.aramaic: מָה קֹדֶשׁ — בֵּין דֶּרֶךְ מִקָּח בֵּין דֶּרֶךְ חִילּוּל,
phrases.english: Just as consecrated property — both by purchase and by redemption,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שְׁבִיעִית — בֵּין דֶּרֶךְ מִקָּח בֵּין דֶּרֶךְ חִילּוּל.
phrases.english: so too Sheviis — both by purchase and by redemption.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel to step 5: gives the verse source for the second opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'קודש' compares שביעית to הקדש, which can be transferred through both methods.

steps.title: What does רבי יוחנן do with the 'selling' verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן uses the joining of the יובל verse to the selling verse, since רבי אלעזר learned his rule from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, what does he do with the verse 'if you sell an item'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן ignores the source רבי אלעזר used. If the closeness of the two פסוקים teaches 'sale only', how does רבי יוחנן explain them?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a rule that no part of a פסוק is wasted. Since רבי יוחנן does not learn 'sale only' from this סמיכות, he must use it for something else. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he do with it? (How does he use this verse?)
'If you sell an item' (ויקרא כה:יד)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan,
this verse 'if you sell an item'
phrases.notes: This is about the two verses sitting side by side (סמיכות), which רבי אלעזר learned from in step 5.

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי ״כִּי תִמְכְּרוּ מִמְכָּר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sources were given, the גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן deals with רבי אלעזר's source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What lesson רבי יוחנן learns from the סמיכות of יובל and selling, since he does not learn 'sale only' from it.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן uses it for the lesson of רבי יוסי בר חנינא
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן needs the סמיכות for רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching: a person who does business with שביעית produce will end up selling his own belongings.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for the teaching of רבי יוסי בר חנינא. As a ברייתא says, רבי יוסי בר חנינא said: Come and see how severe even the 'dust' of שביעית is. A person who trades in שביעית produce will in the end sell his movable property and his vessels. This is shown by the verse 'In this יובל year, each man shall return to his land', and right next to it: 'And if you sell an item to your fellow…'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן uses the same two joined פסוקים for a warning about punishment, not for a rule about how holiness transfers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trading in שביעית produce is only a minor offshoot ('dust') of the שביעית laws, yet its punishment is harsh: the trader becomes poor and must sell his belongings. The joining of 'יובל' with 'if you sell' hints at this. Once the סמיכות teaches this lesson, it cannot also teach רבי אלעזר's 'sale only' rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He needs it (for a different lesson)
The 'dust' of שביעית: a minor or secondary violation of it
Does business, trades
His movable belongings
And right next to it is written (סמיכות פרשיות)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן does NOT argue that the two verses are unconnected. He agrees they are joined on purpose. He just learns a different lesson from that joining: a punishment, not a rule about how holiness transfers.

phrases.aramaic: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא.
phrases.english: He needs it for the teaching of Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yosei bar Chanina said:
Come and see how severe
even the 'dust' of the Sabbatical Year is, etc.
phrases.notes: 'Dust' means a minor or secondary prohibition, such as trading in the produce.

phrases.english: A person who trades in Sabbatical-Year produce

phrases.aramaic: לְסוֹף מוֹכֵר אֶת מִטַּלְטְלָיו וְאֶת כֵּלָיו,
phrases.english: will in the end sell his movable property and his vessels,
as it is said: 'In this year of Jubilee
you shall return, each man to his land,'
and right next to it is written:
'And if you sell an item to your fellow, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר חֲנִינָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יוחנן uses the סמיכות for רבי יוסי בר חנינא's teaching that trading in שביעית produce leads to selling one's belongings.

steps.title: What does רבי אלעזר do with רבי יוחנן's verse?
steps.stepSummary: Now the גמרא asks the reverse: how does רבי אלעזר use 'it is קודש', since he does not learn redemption (חילול) from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר, what does he do with the verse that רבי יוחנן used?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the question around. It asks how רבי אלעזר uses 'it is קודש', the verse רבי יוחנן used to show that חילול works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר holds that transfer works only through a sale, so he does not learn חילול from 'קודש'. The גמרא wants to know what this word teaches him instead.

keyTerms.meaning: This verse

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar,
this verse of Rabbi Yochanan
phrases.notes: Refers to 'כִּי יוֹבֵל הִיא קֹדֶשׁ' from step 6.

phrases.english: what does he do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, הַאי קְרָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same question as step 7, now asked about the other side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי אלעזר uses 'כי יובל היא קודש'.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר learns from it that holiness passes to the money
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר uses 'it is קודש' to teach the basic idea that שביעית holiness attaches to its money (דמים), just as הקדש does.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what a ברייתא teaches: 'For it is יובל, it is קודש.' Just as הקדש passes its holiness onto its money, so does שביעית pass its holiness onto its money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר uses 'קודש' for the basic rule that the money paid for שביעית produce becomes holy too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the money becomes holy. They argue only about HOW: רבי אלעזר says only through a sale, and רבי יוחנן says through חילול as well. רבי אלעזר uses 'קודש' only for the basic fact of transfer, not for the redemption method.

keyTerms.meaning: Catches (transfers its holiness onto) its money or value
Holy item, consecrated property (הקדש)

phrases.english: He needs it for what is taught in a ברייתא:
'For it is a Jubilee, it is holy.'
Just as a holy item passes its holiness onto its money,
so too Sabbatical-Year produce passes its holiness onto its money.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר uses 'קודש' to teach that שביעית holiness transfers to its money at all, not that חילול works.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree that שביעית holiness passes to its money. רבי יוחנן uses the 'selling' verse for a punishment lesson. רבי אלעזר uses 'קודש' only for the basic fact that holiness transfers.

steps.title: There are ברייתות supporting each side
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא announces that one ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר and another supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא is taught in line with רבי אלעזר, and a ברייתא is taught in line with רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא tells us it will now bring outside sources supporting each opinion, starting with רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מחלוקת is not just between two אמוראים. Each view matches an earlier ברייתא. The גמרא now quotes those ברייתות one by one.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא is taught in line with his view

phrases.english: It is taught in a ברייתא in line with Rabbi Elazar,
and it is taught in a ברייתא in line with Rabbi Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, וְתַנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'how does each use the verse' discussion and brings support from ברייתות.
steps.raayaObject: Both opinions in the מחלוקת of step 4.

steps.title: The ברייתא supporting רבי אלעזר: the money becomes forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that just as הקדש passes its holiness to its money and that money is forbidden, so שביעית money becomes forbidden like the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא in line with רבי אלעזר: שביעית passes its holiness onto its money, as it says, 'For it is יובל, it shall be holy to you.' Just as הקדש passes onto its money and the money is forbidden, so too שביעית passes onto its money and the money is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא that supports רבי אלעזר. Its first part says the money received for שביעית produce takes on the produce's restrictions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comparing שביעית to הקדש tells us that the money becomes restricted, just as הקדש money cannot be used for ordinary purposes. The proof for רבי אלעזר comes later, in step 17. There the גמרא points out that every case in this ברייתא uses the word 'לקח' (he bought) and never a redemption.

keyTerms.meaning: And it (the money) is forbidden, held to the produce's restrictions
'It shall be holy to you' (ויקרא כה:יב)

phrases.english: It is taught in line with Rabbi Elazar:
Sabbatical-Year produce passes its holiness onto its money,
as it is said: 'For it is a Jubilee,
it shall be holy to you,'

phrases.aramaic: מָה קֹדֶשׁ תּוֹפֵס אֶת דָּמָיו — וְאָסוּר,
phrases.english: just as a holy item passes onto its money, and that money is forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שְׁבִיעִית תּוֹפֶסֶת אֶת דָּמֶיהָ — וַאֲסוּרָה.
phrases.english: so too Sabbatical-Year produce passes onto its money, and that money is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא כְּווֹתֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: שְׁבִיעִית תּוֹפֶסֶת אֶת דָּמֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the first ברייתא announced in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's view that the transfer is not like redemption (it works only through a sale).
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא comparing שביעית to הקדש only in that the money becomes forbidden.

steps.title: Maybe the produce itself should become ordinary, like redeemed הקדש
steps.stepSummary: Inside the ברייתא, a suggestion: maybe we should extend the comparison, so that the original שביעית produce loses its holiness the way redeemed הקדש does.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or perhaps: just as הקדש passes onto its money and the הקדש item itself becomes ordinary (חולין), so too שביעית passes onto its money and the produce itself becomes ordinary?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake. If שביעית is like הקדש, perhaps the original produce should also become חולין once the money is holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When הקדש is redeemed, its holiness moves over completely: the money becomes holy and the object becomes ordinary. The ברייתא asks whether שביעית works the same way, as a true redemption. This is the הוה אמינא that the next step rejects.

keyTerms.meaning: Or perhaps (introduces a possible wrong conclusion)
Becomes ordinary, non-holy (חולין)

steps.confusionAlert: This is NOT the final law. It is a suggestion the ברייתא raises only in order to reject it in the next line.

phrases.english: Or perhaps: just as a holy item passes onto its money
and itself becomes ordinary,
so too Sabbatical-Year produce passes onto its money
and itself becomes ordinary?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי, מָה קֹדֶשׁ תּוֹפֵס דָּמָיו וְיוֹצֵא לְחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests how far the הקדש comparison of step 12 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: The scope of the comparison between שביעית and הקדש.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, then שביעית produce should become חולין when its holiness passes to the money, as redeemed הקדש does.

steps.title: 'It shall be': the produce stays holy
steps.stepSummary: The word 'תהיה' teaches that the produce stays in its holy state. Only the money becomes holy as well, unlike redemption of הקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'it shall be' (תהיה), meaning: it stays as it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the suggestion. The word 'תהיה' shows that the original שביעית produce keeps its holiness even after the money becomes holy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So שביעית is compared to הקדש only partly. The money becomes forbidden, but the produce does not become חולין. The holiness spreads to the money rather than moving off the produce. The ברייתא now illustrates this with a chain of purchases (steps 15-16).

keyTerms.meaning: The verse teaches (introduces a word that proves the point)
It shall stay in its (holy) state

steps.whatToRemember: שביעית money becomes holy, and the produce stays holy too. The holiness spreads to the money; it does not move off the produce.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that שביעית holiness is unlike הקדש: it spreads to the money instead of moving off the produce. The example of a chain of purchases in the next steps builds on this rule.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: 'it shall be,'
meaning it shall remain in its state.
phrases.notes: The produce stays holy even though the money also became holy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects step 13's suggestion using the word 'תהיה'.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a word in the verse to limit the comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The produce becomes חולין once its holiness transfers, like redeemed הקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce stays holy and the money also becomes holy; the comparison to הקדש does not extend to the produce becoming חולין.

steps.title: The chain of purchases with שביעית money
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא describes a chain of purchases: meat bought with שביעית produce, then fish, then wine, then oil. Each new item takes on the holiness, and the item before it is released.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If someone bought meat with שביעית produce, both the produce and the meat must be removed (ביעור) at the time of removal in שביעית. If he then bought fish with the meat, the meat leaves the holy status and the fish enters it. If he bought wine with the fish, the fish leaves and the wine enters. If he bought oil with the wine, the wine leaves and the oil enters.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the previous steps continues. It now gives a concrete example of how the holiness of שביעית moves from item to item through purchases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first purchase makes the meat holy, and the produce stays holy too, so both must be removed. From then on, each new purchase moves the holiness forward: the new item becomes holy and the item before it becomes ordinary. This matches step 14: the original produce stays holy and only the money gains holiness.

keyTerms.meaning: How so? (introduces an explanation or example)
must be removed (ביעור): once that type of produce is gone from the fields, it may no longer be kept
went out: lost its holy status
entered: took on the holy status

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the original שביעית produce ever 'goes out.' Only the in-between items (meat, fish, wine) leave the holy status. The original produce stays holy forever, and only the latest item bought carries the holiness along with it.

phrases.english: How so?
If he bought meat with Sabbatical-Year produce —
both these and those must be removed in the Sabbatical Year.
phrases.notes: Both the produce and the meat are holy.

phrases.english: If he bought fish with the meat —
the meat goes out and the fish enter.
phrases.notes: The holiness moves from the meat to the fish.

phrases.english: If he bought wine with the fish —
the fish go out and the wine enters.
If he bought oil with the wine —
the wine goes out and the oil enters.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? לָקַח בְּפֵירוֹת שְׁבִיעִית בָּשָׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and illustrates the rule from step 14 with a concrete chain of purchases.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר's position that holiness moves through purchase (מקח)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא on 'כי יובל היא קדש תהיה לכם'

steps.title: Summary rule: the last item is holy, and the original produce stays forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא sums up: whatever was bought last carries the holiness of שביעית, and the original produce itself always stays forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so? The very last item bought enters the holiness of שביעית, and the original produce itself stays forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא closes its example with a short general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two items are holy at any time: the original produce, which never loses its status, and the most recent item bought. Everything in between has been released. This is the 'תהיה' idea from step 14, shown in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: the last one, each time: whatever item is most recent
the original produce itself

steps.whatToRemember: With שביעית, holiness spreads to the money but never leaves the original produce. Only the latest item bought carries it forward.

phrases.aramaic: הָא כֵּיצַד: אַחֲרוֹן אַחֲרוֹן נִכְנָס בַּשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: How so? The last one each time enters the Sabbatical status,
and the produce itself remains forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד: אַחֲרוֹן אַחֲרוֹן נִכְנָס בַּשְּׁבִיעִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the chain of examples in step 15 into one general rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The latest item bought and the original produce are holy. All items in between are released.

steps.title: The word 'bought' shows purchase works but redemption does not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the ברייתא keeps saying 'לקח' (he bought). This shows that holiness moves by purchase (מקח) but not by redemption (חילול), which is רבי אלעזר's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the ברייתא says 'he bought,' 'he bought,' it seems that by way of purchase, yes, the holiness moves. By way of redemption, no.
steps.whatsHappening: This is where the גמרא shows how the ברייתא supports רבי אלעזר. It draws an inference from the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every case in the ברייתא uses the word 'לקח,' meaning an ordinary purchase. It never says 'חילל,' meaning a formal redemption. The גמרא reads this as deliberate: only a purchase moves the holiness of שביעית, as רבי אלעזר holds, and not a redemption, as רבי יוחנן would allow.

keyTerms.meaning: since it teaches: introduces an inference from the wording
apparently / this shows that
by way of a purchase (ordinary buying)
by way of redemption (formally transferring the holiness onto something else)

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the actual proof for רבי אלעזר. It completes the first half of step 11's statement that one ברייתא supports each side.

phrases.english: Since it teaches 'he bought,' 'he bought,'
apparently by way of purchase — yes,
by way of redemption — no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal inference from the ברייתא's wording in steps 15 and 16.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אלעזר: the holiness of שביעית moves only by purchase, not by redemption
steps.raayaSupportSource: The repeated word 'לקח' in the ברייתא

steps.title: A ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן: שביעית can be redeemed onto animals
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says שביעית and מעשר שני produce can be redeemed (מתחללין) onto animals and birds. This shows redemption works for שביעית, as רבי יוחנן holds. רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree only about live animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא supports רבי יוחנן: Both שביעית produce and מעשר שני can be redeemed onto domestic animals, wild animals, and birds, whether alive or slaughtered. That is רבי מאיר's view. The חכמים say: onto slaughtered animals they can be redeemed, but onto live animals they cannot. This is a rabbinic decree, out of concern that the person might raise whole herds from them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now brings the second ברייתא promised in step 11, the one that supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key word is 'מתחללין' (they are redeemed). It shows that the holiness of שביעית can be moved by redemption, not only by purchase. That supports רבי יוחנן. The argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים is only about which animals may be used. The חכמים forbid live animals because the holy animal could breed a whole herd of holy animals.

keyTerms.meaning: a ברייתא is taught in support of him
second tithe: produce that must be eaten in Jerusalem or redeemed for money
they are redeemed: the holiness is transferred onto something else
a rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
herds or flocks

steps.confusionAlert: The disagreement between רבי מאיר and the חכמים is not the proof. Both of them agree that redemption (חילול) works for שביעית. They argue only about live animals. That shared agreement is what supports רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: It is taught in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Both Sabbatical-Year produce and second tithe
are redeemed onto domestic animals, wild animals, and birds,
phrases.notes: The word 'redeemed' is the proof for רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: whether alive or slaughtered,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.
And the Sages say:
onto slaughtered animals — they are redeemed,
onto live animals — they are not redeemed,
a decree, lest he raise herds from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא that supports רבי אלעזר to a second ברייתא that supports רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן: the holiness of שביעית also moves by redemption (חילול)
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא that says 'שביעית ומעשר שני מתחללין על בהמה חיה ועוף'

steps.title: רבא begins to explain the scope of the dispute
steps.stepSummary: רבא opens a statement about the 'dispute' between רבי מאיר and the חכמים. The rest of his statement continues on the next amud.
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. רבא is about to explain exactly where רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree in the ברייתא we just read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא grouped שביעית and מעשר שני together. רבא is about to explain whether the disagreement over live animals really applies to both, or only to one of them. His full statement comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: a dispute or disagreement

phrases.english: Rava said: The dispute
phrases.notes: The statement continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a clarification of the רבי מאיר and חכמים dispute in the ברייתא from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Not yet stated. רבא is beginning to define the scope of the dispute.
